t: Introduction and overview — T-6 Texan II
name: Introduction and overview — T-6 Texan II — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — T-6 Texan II
description: Introduction and overview of the T-6 Texan II: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The T-6 Texan II is a single-engine turboprop trainer built by Beechcraft (Raytheon), entering service in 2000 as the U.S. military's primary flight trainer. About 1,000 have been built for the U.S. and allies; the AT-6 Wolverine light-attack version serves export customers. Baseline facts: Turboprop primary trainer; service from 2000; ~1,000 built by Beechcraft/Raytheon..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
key_points: T-6 Texan II: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history.
Turboprop primary trainer; service from 2000; ~1,000 built by Beechcraft/Raytheon.
